altar noun

also holy table

late Latin

Vulg. Mt. 5.23 (Lewis & Short)
Aug. Conf. 9.11.27

altāre, altāris n.

noun, third declension

The singular is the Vulgate’s and the Church’s; classical Latin has āra, and altāria, plural, for a high altar (Lewis & Short). In Orthodox speech “the altar” is often the whole sanctuary behind the iconostasis, and the table itself the holy table.

Other words

  • āra, ārae f. — an altar (the classical word, of pagan altars)

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Div. 1.101 (Lewis & Short); Liv. 1.7 (Lewis & Short)

  • mēnsa Dominī — the Lord’s table; the holy table

    also used · late Latin · Vulg. 1 Cor. 10.21: mēnsae Dominī participēs esse

Examples

  • tantum illud vōs rogō, ut ad dominī altāre meminerītis meī, ubiubi fuerītis

    only this I ask of you, that you remember me at the Lord’s altar, wherever you may beAug. Conf. 9.11.27

  • Et introībō ad altāre Deī, ad Deum quī laetificat juventūtem meam.

    And I will go in to the altar of God, to God who gives joy to my youth.Vulg. Ps. 42 (43), 4

See also iconostasis, chalice, church, priest.
